What to say: File Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) online through the California Secretary of State bizfile portal. outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN), and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name. What to say: Register online at the Treasurer & Tax Collector's business portal within 30 days of starting business. The fee is tiered by SF gross receipts (e.g. $55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k, each plus a $4 state fee for 2026–27). You will receive a Business Account Number that every city department requires. If the bar's name differs from the LLC name, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail ($60–120), then publish it in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from the Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) and arrange workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund. What to say: Register online at the CDTFA portal for a seller's permit (free, often issued same day) to collect sales tax on food and drinks. CDTFA may request a security deposit depending on projected sales. Then quote workers' compensation insurance (mandatory from the first employee) through a broker or State Compensation Insurance Fund; restaurant class codes typically run 2–6% of payroll. ABC will not issue a liquor license until the seller's permit exists, and city permits ask for proof of workers' comp, so complete both before the ABC application.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Engage an ABC license broker to identify and escrow an existing ABC Type 48 license for transfer to 895 O'Farrell St, or confirm the pathway for a new application if state law allows an exception to the county quota. What to say: Type 48 is a quota license: new ones are only released through ABC's annual priority drawing if the county has headroom; otherwise you buy an existing Type 48 and file a person-to-person and premises-to-premises transfer. Prices in San Francisco run roughly $100k–$450k. Census tract 122.02 is over-concentrated (11 active on-sale licenses vs. 8 authorized), so either a new license or a transfer from outside the tract will require a Public Convenience or Necessity determination from the city. Ask the broker to confirm the pathway and escrow timeline (90–180 days including posting and zoning sign-off), and make the lease contingent on transfer approval. File the ABC application only after the license is in escrow and you have the signed lease, BAN, seller's permit, and entity documents.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Schedule and pass the Department of Public Health pre-opening inspection after DBI plan check approval, then apply for the Health Permit to Operate. What to say: After DPH approves the plans, schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% construction complete and a final inspection when the kitchen is fully installed, finishes are sealed, hand sinks and hot water are operational, and a certified food protection manager is on staff. Book each inspection with your plan reviewer at least two weeks ahead. The permit is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans. The FY 2026–27 fee is $470 for the application with initial inspection, and the annual license fee is $0 for bars through 2026–28. Reinspections are $276/hour, so walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the final inspection to avoid a failed inspection that pushes opening by 2–3 weeks.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Complete Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) training for all alcohol servers and managers, and enroll at least one owner or employee in a food safety manager certification course. What to say: Every alcohol server and manager must complete RBS certification within 60 days of hire under AB 1221: register on the ABC RBS Portal ($3), complete an approved course ($10–25), and pass the exam. Keep the certification list on site for ABC inspections. At least one person must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe, Prometric, NRFSP, 360training; $100–250, 1–14 days) within 60 days of opening; health inspectors ask for the certificate at the pre-opening inspection. All employees who handle food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire ($7–15, online course takes ~2 hours, valid 3 years).
